nature: DEVELOPMENT DIAGNOSTIC on the synthetic fixture. Not a confirmatory experiment: the original draws' test results were already seen (runs/cpu_synthetic_layer_fixture_20260926T152312Z). Population-information arms are oracle diagnostics, not deployable methods.
question: Which of {solver failure, empirical moment estimation, relative-error normalizer estimation, objective/evaluator mismatch} explains the calibration-vs-test gap of minimax_rel (test worst_rel 0.858) vs wrrr_uniform_rel (0.685)?

fixed_from_fixture.note: teachers = the three problem instances of the recorded run (adapters, input distributions, dims, LoRA rank, k, n_cal=32 unchanged). Teachers are different problems, NOT independent seeds of one problem.

resample_stream: _sub_rng(teacher_seed, 'x', task, 'cal_resample', resample_seed), n_cal = 32 per task, same generator distribution

include_original_draw.label: orig_seen
include_original_draw.note: the recorded run's calibration draw; its test results were already seen; reported separately, not pooled with new resamples

arm_definitions.population moment: Sigma_t = E[x x^T] = L_t L_t^T (generator mean is exactly 0; verified by Monte Carlo before use)
arm_definitions.empirical normalizer: E_hat_t = tr(D_t Sigma_hat_t D_t^T) from the same calibration draw
arm_definitions.pop_moment__pop_norm: uses no calibration samples: identical for every draw; computed once per teacher

solver: unchanged from configs/cpu_synthetic.json (dual iters 300, polish 200, refine settings, wrrr_mode pd)
primary_evaluation: population worst-task relative functional error F_pop(M) = max_t tr((M-D_t) Sigma_t (M-D_t)^T) / E_t, identical for all arms
secondary_evaluation: original test-sample worst/mean relative error (n_test=512, PREVIOUSLY SEEN, development diagnostic only)
stored_diagnostics: per-task empirical fit errors and population errors
lambda at the best lower bound
whitened singular values sigma_k, sigma_k+1 and uniqueness
independent Izenman raw-data RRR at lambda*: M and g discrepancy
CPU process time per fit, number of WRRR solves

decision_rules.delta: Delta = F_pop(minimax_rel) - F_pop(wrrr_uniform_rel) per (teacher, new resample)
decision_rules.problem_present: mean Delta over the 9 new cells > +0.02 AND teacher-level mean Delta > 0 for >= 2 of 3 teachers
decision_rules.problem_absent: mean Delta over the 9 new cells <= 0
decision_rules.pop_moment__pop_norm: fit objective equals the evaluation objective, so minimax must satisfy F_pop(minimax) <= F_pop(uniform) + its own UB-LB gap; a violation means solver/objective/evaluator mismatch and is investigated, not explained away
decision_rules.solver_failure_refuted_for_a_fit: gap_rel <= 1e-6 AND independent Izenman g at lambda* agrees within 1e-9 relative AND rank(M) <= k

attribution.moment_noise: problem present in emp_moment arms and absent in both pop_moment arms
attribution.normalizer_noise: problem absent in emp_moment__pop_norm while present in emp_moment__emp_norm
attribution.cause_undetermined: any other pattern; reported as undetermined

resource_caps.enforcement: RLIMIT_CPU (hard) and RLIMIT_AS set in-process before any work; soft check before each fit marks remaining cells NOT_RUN_CAP
resource_caps.installs: none required (pure-Python stdlib); install/download cost recorded as zero

monte_carlo_check.tolerance: max |Sigma_mc - Sigma|_ij <= 6 * sqrt((Sigma_ii Sigma_jj + Sigma_ij^2) / n)
